MASTER PROMPT — JOB-SPECIFIC RESUME OPTIMIZATION

I will provide you with a JOB TITLE and JOB DESCRIPTION. Your task is to create a highly targeted resume section specifically for that vacancy.

IMPORTANT:
Do not give me generic resume content.
Do not simply rewrite or copy the job description.
Do not use complicated or overly formal English.
Do not invent unrealistic responsibilities, achievements, tools, certifications, employers, or experience that are not reasonable for the candidate.
Do not claim that I have skills or experience that clearly conflict with the information available in the conversation.
Use the job description to identify the employer's real priorities and then connect my relevant skills and experience to those priorities.

Your goal is to make the resume look like it was written specifically for this company and this vacancy.

==================================================
1. PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
==================================================

Write ONLY TWO PARAGRAPHS.

The Professional Summary must be based on research about the company whenever the company name is available.

You MUST research the company online before writing the summary.

Research:
• What the company actually does
• Its products/services/business model
• Its industry
• Its customers or market where relevant
• Its major business priorities
• The main operational or role-related challenges/pain points that are reasonably connected to the vacancy
• What the company would likely value from someone in this position

Do not give me a generic description of the company.
Do not invent secret or unsupported internal problems.
Pain points should be realistic and clearly connected to the company's business and the supplied job description.

PARAGRAPH 1 — COMPANY + PAIN POINTS

Start naturally with:

"After researching "[Company Name]"..."

The company name must be:
BOLD ONLY

Do NOT italicize the company name.

Immediately after mentioning the company, explain what the company does and its important business priorities.

The FIRST important sentence or key statement after the company name must be:
BOLD + ITALIC

Then explain the most relevant business/role challenges.

Focus on approximately 2–4 important pain points rather than listing everything.

Examples of pain points:
• slow processes
• inaccurate data
• poor follow-up
• manual work
• quality issues
• customer retention
• lead generation
• recruitment delays
• weak reporting
• poor coordination
• operational inefficiency
• software defects
• delayed feedback
• inventory problems
• compliance issues
• performance gaps
• high workload
• customer experience issues

Only use pain points that make sense for the company and the role.

PARAGRAPH 2 — HOW I WILL HELP

Start with:

"As a [Job Title], I will help address these challenges by..."

This ENTIRE opening sentence must be:
BOLD + ITALIC

Then explain clearly and naturally:

• what I will do
• what problems I will help solve
• what processes I will improve
• what tools/skills I will use
• how my work will support the team
• what business result I will contribute toward

The paragraph should sound like a real candidate explaining how they can contribute.

Do NOT write exaggerated claims such as:
"I will transform the company"
"I will guarantee 100% success"
"I will increase revenue by 50%"

Use realistic language such as:
• help improve
• support
• reduce delays
• improve accuracy
• keep processes organized
• identify issues early
• support better decisions
• improve customer experience
• maintain reliable records
• help the team meet deadlines

The language must be SIMPLE, NATURAL, HUMAN, and PROFESSIONAL.

Avoid typical AI-sounding phrases such as:
"results-driven professional"
"dynamic individual"
"passionate professional"
"proven track record"
"leverage my expertise"
"synergize"
"robust"
"seamless"
"multifaceted"
unless genuinely necessary.

The summary should feel like:
"I researched your company, I understand what is important to you, I understand where the job can face problems, and here is how I can help."

==================================================
2. PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY FORMATTING
==================================================

Use this exact visual emphasis style:

Heading:
PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY

Normal body text:
10 pt style

Important emphasized text:
11 pt style equivalent

Company name:
BOLD ONLY

First important/key sentence in Paragraph 1:
BOLD + ITALIC

Opening sentence of Paragraph 2:
BOLD + ITALIC

Do NOT make the complete summary bold.

Do NOT italicize the company name.

Example:

After researching **"Company Name"**, ***I understand that the company ...*** The company...

***As a Job Title, I will help address these challenges by...*** I will...

The actual final answer can use Markdown bold and italics to represent this formatting.

==================================================
3. TECHNICAL SKILLS
==================================================

After the Professional Summary, create:

TECHNICAL SKILLS

Provide ONLY 5–6 skills/categories.

Never provide 8, 10, 12 or more skills.

Each skill must be highly relevant to the job description.

Use this format:

• **Skill Category:** Specific skills/tools/tasks.

Examples:

• **Recruitment & Talent Sourcing:** Candidate sourcing, screening, LinkedIn, job portals, pipeline management and follow-ups.

• **Microsoft Excel & Reporting:** Spreadsheets, formulas, data tracking, reporting, dashboards and data analysis.

Do not include irrelevant skills merely to make the section longer.

Prioritize the employer's most important requirements.

Use the exact technology/tool names from the job description when appropriate, but do not falsely claim advanced expertise.

==================================================
4. EXPERIENCE
==================================================

Create ONE highly relevant experience entry.

Use a realistic job title related to the vacancy.

Format:

EXPERIENCE

**[Relevant Job Title]** | **[Company Name]**                                      *[Month Year – Month Year]*

Then provide a MAXIMUM OF 5 bullet points.

Use the symbol:

▸

Each bullet should be concise, professional and action-oriented.

The experience must be tailored to the target position.

Translate the candidate's relevant previous work into responsibilities that demonstrate transferable skills for the target vacancy.

For example:
• Recruitment job → HR/Operations/Marketplace/Customer roles
• Computer Operator → Administrative/Desk Officer roles
• Accounts Assistant → Accounts/Credit/Finance roles
• QA Engineer → Software QA/Test roles
• Sales → Marketing/Business Development/Customer roles

Do not copy the job description line by line.

Do not repeat the same idea in different bullets.

Each bullet should ideally show one of:
• responsibility
• technical skill
• coordination
• problem solving
• accuracy
• reporting
• customer interaction
• performance
• process improvement
• business support

Keep bullets realistic.

==================================================
5. JOB DESCRIPTION ANALYSIS
==================================================

Before writing the resume content, internally identify:

A. Top 5 requirements
B. Top 5 responsibilities
C. Important tools/software
D. Important soft skills
E. Business pain points
F. What the hiring manager most likely wants to see
G. Keywords useful for ATS screening

Then use these findings to create the final resume.

Do not show this analysis unless I ask for it.

==================================================
6. COMPANY RESEARCH RULES
==================================================

When a company is provided:

Research the company online using reliable and current sources.

Prefer:
• Official company website
• Official company careers page
• Official LinkedIn/company profile
• Annual reports
• Official press releases
• Reliable business publications

Do not rely entirely on job-board summaries.

Use research to understand:
• business model
• services/products
• market
• current direction
• role relevance
• realistic pain points

Do not manufacture company facts.

If reliable information about the company cannot be verified, say so internally and keep the company description conservative rather than inventing details.

==================================================
7. JOB-SPECIFIC LANGUAGE
==================================================

Use keywords naturally from the job description.

For ATS compatibility, include relevant terms such as:
• tools
• systems
• technical skills
• reporting
• coordination
• customer service
• data
• KPIs
• compliance
• testing
• recruiting
• sales
• operations
etc.

But do NOT keyword-stuff.

The resume should still sound natural to a human recruiter.

==================================================
8. WRITING STYLE
==================================================

Use:
• Simple English
• Natural English
• Beginner/intermediate English level
• Professional tone
• Clear sentences
• Direct language
• Human wording
• Short to medium sentences
• Strong but realistic language

Avoid:
• unnecessary corporate jargon
• overly complex vocabulary
• long sentences
• fake achievements
• exaggerated claims
• repetitive phrases
• generic career objectives
• obvious AI language

The recruiter should feel:
"This candidate understands our company and understands what this role needs."

==================================================
9. EXPERIENCE TRUTHFULNESS
==================================================

The candidate has real prior work experience.

Write the experience in a way that is highly relevant to the target vacancy while staying believable.

You may emphasize transferable responsibilities and skills that naturally connect to the new job.

Do NOT fabricate:
• companies
• degrees
• certifications
• years of experience
• software expertise
• management level
• achievements
• projects
• numerical results

If placeholders are necessary, use:
[Company Name]
[Month Year – Month Year]

==================================================
10. FINAL OUTPUT FORMAT
==================================================

Return ONLY:

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY

[2 paragraphs exactly]

TECHNICAL SKILLS

• **Skill 1:** ...
• **Skill 2:** ...
• **Skill 3:** ...
• **Skill 4:** ...
• **Skill 5:** ...
• **Skill 6:** ...

EXPERIENCE

**[Relevant Job Title]** | **[Company Name]**        *[Month Year – Month Year]*

▸ ...
▸ ...
▸ ...
▸ ...
▸ ...

No extra explanation.
No "Here is your resume."
No conclusion.
No cover letter.
No interview tips.

==================================================
11. IMPORTANT STYLE RULE
==================================================

The Professional Summary MUST always follow this exact logic:

PARAGRAPH 1:
COMPANY → WHAT THEY DO → THEIR BUSINESS PRIORITIES → THEIR ROLE-RELATED PAIN POINTS

PARAGRAPH 2:
MY ROLE → HOW I WILL HELP → WHAT I WILL DO → WHAT PROBLEMS I WILL REDUCE → BUSINESS VALUE

The summary should be specific enough that it could NOT easily be used for another company.

==================================================
12. INPUT
==================================================

I will now provide:

JOB TITLE:
[Insert job title]

COMPANY:
[Insert company name]

JOB DESCRIPTION:
[Paste complete job description here]

Use the above instructions and create the final targeted resume sections.
